article.title: How to Unclog a Toilet Without a Plunger
article.summary: No plunger? Stop the overflow, then try dish soap and hot water, a wire hanger wrapped in a rag, or a wet-dry vacuum, and know when to call a plumber.
article.body:
Most toilet clogs are soft waste and too much paper stuck in the toilet's built-in trap. You can often clear them without a plunger. This guide starts with the gentlest method and works up.

Affiliate disclosure: some links in this guide are affiliate links. If you buy through them, we may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. We only recommend products we'd use ourselves.

Safety: wear gloves. Don't use boiling water, because it can crack the porcelain bowl. Don't pour chemical drain cleaner into a toilet: it can splash back on you and damage pipes and seals.

Steps

  1. Stop the overflow

    If the bowl is close to the rim, take the tank lid off and push the flapper down to stop more water from flowing in, then turn the shut-off valve behind the toilet clockwise. Lay towels on the floor.

    Done right: the water level in the bowl has stopped rising.

  2. Try dish soap and hot water

    If the bowl is very full, bail some water into a bucket. Squirt about 1/4 cup of liquid dish soap into the bowl and let it sink for 10 minutes. Then pour in about half a gallon of hot tap water from waist height. Wait another 10 to 15 minutes.

    Done right: the water level drops on its own with a gurgle.

  3. Use a toilet auger or a wrapped hanger

    A toilet auger is the right tool if you have one: feed the cable into the drain opening and crank it until the clog breaks. Without one, straighten a wire hanger, wrap the end tightly with a rag and tape so it can't scratch the porcelain, and push it gently into the drain opening to break up the clog.

    Done right: you feel the clog give way and the water drains.

  4. Try a wet-dry vacuum

    A wet-dry vacuum can pull a clog out. Empty the bowl water into a bucket with the vacuum, push the hose into the drain opening, wrap an old towel around it to seal, and turn it on.

    Done right: the vacuum pulls the blockage free.

  5. Test with a flush

    Open the shut-off valve again and let the tank fill. Flush once while watching the bowl, with your hand ready to push the flapper down if it rises.

    Done right: the bowl drains fully and refills to its normal level.

Call a plumber if: several drains are slow or backing up at once, water comes up in a tub or shower when you flush, a hard object such as a toy went down, or nothing has worked after an hour. Those point to a blockage farther down the line.

FAQ

Does dish soap and hot water really unclog a toilet?

For soft clogs of waste and paper, often yes. The soap lubricates and the warm water helps break it down. It won't move a solid object.

Can I use boiling water to unclog a toilet?

No. Boiling water can crack the porcelain bowl. Hot tap water is enough.

Is it safe to use drain cleaner in a toilet?

It's best avoided. Chemical drain cleaners can splash, damage pipes and seals, and make the job dangerous if you then need to plunge or snake.

What is a toilet auger?

A short, crank-operated cable with a protective sleeve that won't scratch the bowl. It's the most effective tool for stubborn toilet clogs.
